claims.evidence: NHS prevention page: weight-bearing and resistance exercise, vitamin D supplement/sunlight, smoking, alcohol 14 units. Inactivity as a risk factor appears only in a trust list (Calderdale), not the NHS page text returned.
claims.newSentence: NHS pages link bone health to weight-bearing exercise, calcium, vitamin D, not smoking and keeping alcohol low.

claims.evidence: NHS: weight-bearing and resistance exercise are 'particularly important for improving bone density'. 'Most useful' overstates.
claims.newSentence: NHS guidance describes weight-bearing and resistance exercise as particularly important for bone strength.

claims.evidence: NHS Tayside leaflet and ROS/NHS pages: body needs vitamin D to absorb calcium from food; dietary calcium and vitamin D emphasised for bone health.

Calderdale trust and ROS list low body weight/BMI, lack of activity, smoking, excess alcohol. Overweight is not supported: research summary shows lowest fracture risk in overweight people, and no NHS text lists overweight.
claims.newSentence: Being inactive, having a low body weight, smoking and heavy drinking are listed as risk factors for weaker bones.

claims.evidence: NHS bone health over 65: strength activities at least twice a week; balance and flexibility work twice a week.
As c02: NHS says 'particularly important for improving bone density'.
claims.newSentence: NHS guidance describes weight-bearing and resistance exercise as particularly important for improving bone density.

claims.evidence: NHS prevention: high-impact weight-bearing exercise such as running, skipping, dancing, aerobics and jumping on the spot strengthen muscles, ligaments and joints.
NHS prevention: swimming and cycling are not weight-bearing; NHS inform: good for fitness but do not build bone density as effectively.
Only 'lack of physical activity' as a risk factor is in returned text (Calderdale trust). Muscle and bone loss and falls mechanism was not stated.
claims.newSentence: Lack of physical activity is listed as a risk factor for osteoporosis.

claims.evidence: NHS prevention returned text says adults need 700mg calcium a day, which should be obtainable from the daily diet. 'Important for maintaining bone health' not shown verbatim.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says most adults should be able to get the calcium they need from their daily diet.

claims.evidence: NHS: difficult to get enough vitamin D from food alone, so consider a daily supplement. Dose is not to be given in prose; 'for people at risk' not what the page said (it was for adults generally).
claims.newSentence: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium, and the NHS says it can be difficult to get enough vitamin D from food alone, so a daily supplement may be considered.

claims.evidence: NHS: sunlight from late March/early April to end of September triggers vitamin D production; consider a daily supplement. 'All adults ... October to March' came from NHS Tayside, not the cited NHS page.
claims.newSentence: Sunlight from about late March or early April to the end of September helps the body make vitamin D, and the NHS suggests considering a daily vitamin D supplement.

claims.evidence: Only underweight/low BMI supported as a risk factor (Calderdale trust). Osteopenia described by NHS 111 Wales as bone loss before osteoporosis. Overweight not supported.
claims.newSentence: Osteopenia is the stage of bone loss before osteoporosis, and being underweight is listed among the risk factors for bone loss.

claims.evidence: NHS 111 Wales: smoking linked to higher osteoporosis risk; advises not more than 14 units alcohol a week; Calderdale trust lists excess alcohol; NHS prevention covers cutting alcohol.
Royal Osteoporosis Society says excess salt may increase urinary calcium loss. It was not in the cited NHS page text, and ROS says 'may'.
claims.newSentence: The Royal Osteoporosis Society says too much salt may increase the amount of calcium lost in urine.

claims.evidence: NHS bone health over 65: muscle-strengthening at least twice a week; balance and flexibility twice a week.
NHS over-65 page: 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, spread across the week. 'Built up gradually' not in returned text.
claims.newSentence: It also advises 150 minutes (2 and a half hours) of moderate-intensity activity a week, ideally spread across the days.

claims.evidence: Statement came from NHS 111 Wales (talk to GP or health specialist before a new exercise programme after diagnosis); ROS says most can exercise safely and advises a doctor or physio if many fractures. The cited NHS prevention page text did not show it.
claims.newSentence: NHS 111 Wales suggests that people diagnosed with osteoporosis talk to a GP or health specialist before starting a new exercise programme.

claims.evidence: NHS DEXA page: a scan is often used to help diagnose osteoporosis or assess risk. 'The standard test' not stated.
claims.newSentence: A DEXA bone density scan is often used to help diagnose osteoporosis or to assess the risk of it.

notes: Overweight as a bone risk is not backed by returned UK text and research summaries suggest a more complex picture, so it was dropped from c04/c13. Vitamin D dose (10 micrograms) removed from prose per writing rules. No urgency statements in this guide. 9/9 searches used.
